title: Snapdragon laptop punt proves great for battery work time but comes with BIOS time issues
body:
This laptop is excellent for battery life and generally works well with most Office / Adobie apps I use along simple games.  I have found the AI engagement has been quick and useful even when running several apps the  processor remains cool and the fan hardly ever kicks in compaired to my old Intel I5 laptop. The HP physical build and erganomices are to the expected high standard. Its still fairly early days for my Snapdragon laptop and the experience is not without some irritations.

The  irritations: 
1. The bios clock is set to USA CET and no matter how many times I change it the BIOS will not save the change.  This means on boot, opening up the pc etc the clock is wrong and you have to wait for Mircrosoft to sync with the internet for the time to alter to GMT.   I have got used to this for general use but for offline work its an issue . I have to manually change the time before saving documents that occasionally require version histories, if you forget sometime the time and date will be 8 hours ahead which I have found can cause issues 
with change histories on documents.   
2.  I have had to revet to Outlook old version as the new preinstalled version kept refusing to selete  emails or remove emails to the recycle bin. so you delete 20  emails and then next time you start outlook they would return as new emails.  After 3 reinstalls of new outlook  over a couple of weeks I gave up and installed the old outlook format and have had no issues since. 

Overall the laptop was purchased on the battery duration requirement and cooler running, for general home and small business use.  Once you get past the time issues that may will go away after HP do some future BIOS updates it is a great tool.
product_name: HP OmniBook 5 16" 2K Laptop, Snapdragon X, 16GB RAM, 256GB SSD

title: Georgous OLED screen, good battery life, Snap Dragon handles multi-tasks well
body:
I have had good experiences with HP laptops - and this one is no exception. Keyboard has a good feel, and 2 level backlight. Touch pad is very spacious, and also is responsive. The screen is a brilliant OLED, so colors really pop - great for streaming. Don't let the 300 nits spec fool you - it is plenty bright for indoor use.
The Snap Dragon processor requires less power, so even though it is a 16 inch display, I expect to get 8 hours or more with just the usual internet, videos, etc. Of course, will depend on screen brightness, and processing demands. The processor handles multiple tasks well, and doesn't seem to slow down. I do recommend getting rid of all the extra "junk" that comes preinstalled. 
This would definitely benefit from either a 1Tb SSD, or a micro SD slot for additional storage. 

At full price it is a little pricey but still a good buy, and if you catch it on sale, it is a steal.....

title: Lightweight laptop that handles work, gaming and A
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Really impressed with this laptop. It looks sleek, thin, and lightweight but still feels solid. It runs on Windows 11 and handles apps like Microsoft Teams, Word, Outlook, and Excel really smoothly, even with several tabs open at once. The 1080p picture quality on YouTube is great - bright and sharp, and the OLED screen makes videos look really smooth, even in fast action scenes.

I didn't buy it for gaming, but I've tried Roblox, Call of Duty, and Elder Scrolls, and they all played brilliantly with no lag or glitches. I was especially impressed with Call of Duty — even during the fast shooting action sequences, the graphics were super smooth and responsive, which I didn't expect from such a slim laptop. The sound is good too, even though the speakers are on the bottom. You get one USB-A port (handy for a mouse) and two USB-C ports for everything else. 

The AI features built into the Snapdragon X16 really stand out, helping apps run more efficiently, optimizing performance, and speeding up tasks with minimal battery impact. It's easy to access at any time using the dedicated AI button, which lets you ask questions, get instant answers, and analyze files directly on your device as well as troubleshooting. 

The battery easily lasts all day, which makes it perfect for students or anyone who needs a reliable laptop to carry around.

title: I am not disappointed
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I bought this because I was reliant on my work laptop all the time. I wanted my own laptop to keep photos, music tabs, and to do my guitar lessons. In terms of screen size, as I don't intend on carrying around I opted for the larger screen.
First off, the laptop itself is sleek in design, it looks really nice. The initial set up is very easy as the instructions are very straight forward to follow and it did not take long at all. I'm new to Windows 11 so that took a bit of getting used to, but once I got by that, personalising the laptop was very easy to pick up. When you log on it loads up very quick which is a bonus.
I use this for guitar lessons, and can say the sound is clear, and the video is very sharp; the larger screen helps with the video call for sure.
In terms of ports, there are 2 usb-c's that can be used as inputs and outputs (1 for a charger if using plugged in), if you need to have more connections or connect a monitor there are universal hubs that can be sourced, this is something I have personally done myself. I feel the laptop could have done with an HDMI, but it's not a show stopper.
Last, but not least, the battery - I've not used it a great deal without the charger being plugged in, but so far it appears to hold a good charge. For me and what I use it for, overall this laptop is great, only let down for is the minimal amount of ports, but that's easy remedied.
